{"answer":"Use Query-Aware Flow Diffusion RAG (QAFD-RAG) to find query-relevant evidence subgraphs without training: it is a training-free framework that dynamically weights edges during traversal based on alignment with the query’s embedding, recovering relevant subgraphs with high probability and providing statistical retrieval guarantees. It is designed to avoid irrelevant but structurally connected regions by adapting exploration to each query’s holistic semantics. [3]

If you need a “best evidence” subgraph even when the knowledge graph is a black box with unknown schema, BubbleRAG formalizes retrieval as Optimal Informative Subgraph Retrieval and provides a training-free pipeline to optimize recall and precision via candidate evidence graph discovery, composite ranking, and reasoning-aware expansion. This directly targets selecting informative evidence subgraphs under black-box constraints. [5]

If your setting is “hidden KG” but you specifically want a compact, label-free selector for informationally sufficient and structurally minimal subgraphs, GFM-Retriever uses a pre-trained Graph Foundation Model as a cross-domain retriever and then derives a label-free subgraph selector optimized by an Information Bottleneck objective to produce a minimal “core set” of golden evidence for the query. [1]

These differ in guarantees and assumptions: QAFD-RAG emphasizes training-free query-aware traversal with retrieval probability guarantees; BubbleRAG emphasizes black-box schema handling and explicit recall/precision optimization; GFM-Retriever emphasizes an Information Bottleneck-based label-free minimal subgraph selection on top of Graph Foundation Model retrieval. [1,3,5]","grounded":true}
